resumeText:
Omar Khalil
Backend Engineer
omar.khalil@example.com | Amman, Jordan

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with four years building and operating REST APIs in Java. Most
of my work has been on Spring Boot services backed by MongoDB, shipped as Docker
containers. I like owning a service end to end, including the boring parts:
error handling, timeouts, and what happens when a dependency is down.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Backend Engineer, Nimbus Logistics
2023 - present
- Own three Spring Boot services handling shipment tracking, roughly 400 requests
  per second at peak.
- Designed the MongoDB schema and indexes for the tracking collection after query
  latency became the bottleneck; p99 dropped from 800ms to 60ms.
- Built the integration layer that calls our pricing service over HTTP, including
  retry with backoff and a circuit breaker so a slow dependency degrades instead
  of cascading.
- Introduced contract tests between services after a field rename broke
  production on a Friday.

Backend Engineer, Cedar Systems
2021 - 2023
- Built REST APIs in Java and Spring Boot for an internal HR product.
- Implemented JWT authentication and role-based access control across eight
  endpoints.
- Containerised the service with Docker and wrote the Compose setup the team
  still uses locally.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers against a real MongoDB instance.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science, University of Jordan, 2021

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Java, Spring Boot, MongoDB, Docker, REST API design, JUnit, Testcontainers,
Maven, Git, Linux
jobDescription: We are hiring a backend engineer to design, build and maintain the REST APIs behind our recruitment platform. You will own services end to end: schema design, endpoint implementation, authentication, and the deployment pipeline that ships them. Day to day you will be writing Java against Spring Boot, modelling data in MongoDB, and packaging services with Docker. We care about clear API contracts, tests that catch real regressions, and services that fail in understandable ways. Experience integrating with internal services over HTTP and handling partial failures gracefully is particularly relevant, since our platform coordinates several services that can each be slow or unavailable.
